title: Watch: Arizona Governor-Aligned Canvassers Caught Willing To Allow Noncitizens To Vote
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Watch: Arizona Governor-Aligned Canvassers Caught Willing To
hay:
watch: arizona governor-aligned canvassers caught willing to allow noncitizens to vote watch: arizona governor-aligned canvassers caught willing to allow noncitizens to vote

submitted by muckraker,

canvassers registering voters for groups backing arizona gov. katie hobbs's re-election told undercover muckraker journalists posing as a non-citizen and as a felon on probation that they could go ahead and register to vote, hidden-camera footage shows.

with the midterm elections weeks away, muckraker visited voter registration drives run by three democrat-aligned organizations: stand indivisible arizona, worker power, and the democratic national committee's when we count program. at each, a muckraker journalist told the canvasser they were not eligible to vote. muckraker also attended an afl-cio phone bank mobilizing voters for hobbs, where a journalist volunteering to make calls asked whether voters' citizenship mattered.

muckraker stopped every exercise before any voter registration form was submitted.

breaking: katie hobbs-aligned canvassers caught willing to allow non-citizens and a felon to vote muckraker went undercover in arizona to investigate the groups working to re-elect gov. katie hobbs @katiehobbs and other democrats. here’s what we found: stand indivisible arizona (endorsed gov. hobbs in their 2026 ballot guide) — our journalist posed as a canadian citizen and asked to register to vote. the canvasser not only agreed to help the alleged non-citizen register, but when asked whether other canadians could register too, she said, “tell them to do it online.” worker power (working to re-elect gov. hobbs) — our journalist told a canvasser they were not a u.s. citizen. despite this, at our journalist’s request, the canvasser marked “yes” on the citizenship question of the voter registration form. when we count (the dnc’s own registration program) — our journalist posed as a felon on probation and asked to register to vote. the canvassers looked up the law and saw that a felon on probation is ineligible. even so, they encouraged our journalist to register: “you should just do it.” afl-cio (phone bank mobilizing voters for gov. hobbs) — our undercover journalist asked a phone bank trainer whether to ask the people being called if they're citizens. the trainer’s answer: “we don’t care.” our journalists stopped every exercise before any voter registration form was submitted. we also asked gov. katie hobbs about these findings. watch this report and share it with the world.

— muckraker (@realmuckraker) october 22, 2026

stand indivisible arizona: "take this and tell them to do it online"

stand indivisible arizona, a nonprofit that has endorsed hobbs and other democrats running in 2026, was running a voter registration drive at paradise valley community college. a muckraker journalist, posing as a canadian student in the u.s. on an f-1 visa, approached a canvasser.

when the canvasser was told that the journalist was a canadian on a student visa, she first said, "we can't do it." but when the journalist asked, "can i just fill it out, submit it with you, and then forget it?" she answered: "yeah, i guess. the other thing you could do is you could go online, but i'd rather do it with you."

asked whether the journalist's canadian friends could register to vote too, she said: "take this [a business card with a qr code linking to an online voter registration form] and tell them to do it online."

when muckraker's anthony rubin returned to ask about the exchange, she said, "i told you, i can't stop you from putting it online," and declined further comment.

worker power: "okay, if you want to"

worker power is a phoenix-based nonprofit that raised nearly $10 million in the 2024 election cycle and says it runs the largest electoral field program in arizona. this year it is working to re-elect hobbs and other democrats. muckraker found a canvasser registering voters at the phoenix public library and again posed as a non-citizen.

"are you a usa citizen?" the canvasser asked.

"not yet," the journalist said.

"you have to be a usa citizen to vote," she replied. the journalist said they were a resident and asked to "just send it." she asked, "are you sure you want to try it?" then said, "okay, if you want to," and marked "yes" for u.s. citizenship on the arizona voter registration form.

"yes, and then you need to sign there," she said.

approached afterward, she declined to say how often non-citizens are registered.

when we count: "you should just do it"

when we count is the dnc's own voter registration program, the largest in the party's history. it launched in arizona in 2026 and pays young fellows to register new democratic voters. muckraker found its canvassers at mesa community college, where journalist anthony rubin posed as a felon on probation.

under arizona law, a felony conviction suspends the right to vote (a.r.s. § 13-904). the canvassers looked it up. "you're restored to vote when probation has been completed," one said.

asked whether they cared if the journalist registered anyway, one said, "you should just do it. just do it."

when rubin returned to ask how often the group helps ineligible people register, the canvassers declined to comment and left.

afl-cio phone bank: "not our business"

muckraker also attended an afl-cio phone bank at a union hall in central phoenix, where volunteers were phone banking to mobilize voters to support katie hobbs.

a muckraker journalist asked the phone bank trainer whether to ask the people being called if they were citizens. "no, we don't get into any of that," the trainer said. "we don't care."

"if he's not a u.s. citizen, why should i proceed?" the journalist asked. "not our business," the trainer said.

gov. hobbs: no comment

katie hobbs later spoke in the same building as the afl-cio phone bank at an event hosted by afscme, one of the unions endorsing her re-election. anthony rubin asked her about non-citizens being registered to vote and about the groups working for her re-election. she did not respond

what the law says

no arizona law requires voter registration drives to verify citizenship; county recorders check eligibility after forms are submitted. but arizona law makes it a class 6 felony for anyone who "knowingly causes or procures another person to be registered" while "knowing that such other person is not entitled to such registration" (a.r.s. § 16-182).

title: Ex-FBI "Shadow Government" Official Among Two Charged With Lying To Congress Over Hunter Biden Laptop
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Ex-FBI "Shadow Government" Official Among Two Charged With L
hay:
ex-fbi "shadow government" official among two charged with lying to congress over hunter biden laptop ex-fbi "shadow government" official among two charged with lying to congress over hunter biden laptop

two former senior fbi officials who ran the bureau's now-defunct foreign influence task force during the 2020 election were charged friday with lying to congress about their roles in the fbi's hunter biden investigations.

nikki cole floris, 46, and bradley benavides, 56, each face one count of lying to congress in a criminal complaint, d.c. u.s. attorney jeanine pirro announced in a post on x. both surrendered friday and made their first appearance in federal court in washington, according to the ap.

floris led the task force as a deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022, while benavides was its section chief through the 2020 election, fbi director kash patel said. both testified that the fitf was not involved in the hunter biden investigations. "documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications, and witness accounts contradict their testimony," patel wrote, crediting the bureau's kansas city field office alongside the justice department and pirro.

two former senior fbi officials, nikki cole floris and bradley benavides, were taken into custody today on charges of allegedly lying to congress about their involvement in the fbi's investigations into hunter biden. the charges stem from an ongoing investigation into the since-dissolved fbi foreign influence task force. floris led the fitf as a deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. benavides was the fitf section chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election. both testified that the fitf was not involved in the hunter biden investigations. documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications, and witness accounts contradict their testimony. floris is also on record privately claiming to be "running a shadow government" during the 2020 election in her role on the fitf. lying to congress by senior fbi officials strikes at the heart of our system. no one is above the law. the fbi has already dismantled the corrupt cr-15 squad that engaged in political weaponization targeting their opponents, including president trump. thanks to @thejusticedept @fbikansascity and @usattypirro . -dkp

— fbi director kash patel (@fbidirectorkash) october 23, 2026

benavides told congress he learned about the laptop story from wikipedia, but the justice department says it has evidence he discussed it with others inside the fbi, fox news reports. prosecutors also say floris discussed hunter biden with members of the task force despite testifying otherwise. pirro said the evidence showed "their involvement in helping shape the public narrative about hunter biden's laptop right before the election."

floris' lawyers called her "a patriot" who served as an fbi intelligence officer for nearly 20 years and said the justice department accused her "on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts." "it's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election," they said in a statement. benavides has not publicly commented.

the case lands less than two weeks before the nov. 3 midterms, the latest in a series of politically charged justice department actions in the run-up to the vote, the ap noted.

what the task force knew

christopher wray set up the task force in 2017 to counter foreign influence operations, and it served as the bureau's line to social media companies ahead of the 2020 election. the task force knew the laptop was real when the new york post began publishing its contents in october 2020, laura dehmlow, then the fitf's section chief, told house judiciary investigators in july 2023, the free beacon reported.

the fbi nonetheless refused to answer social media companies' questions about the laptop, including from a twitter employee who asked task force representatives about its authenticity at a previously scheduled meeting the day the post story ran, according to the committee.

benavides also crossed paths with the two republican senators then digging into the biden family's foreign money. on aug. 6, 2020, he briefed sens. chuck grassley and ron johnson in a session that, according to a june 2023 letter from house judiciary chairman jim jordan, hampered their investigation into hunter biden's financial connections. grassley called the briefing "unnecessary and completely irrelevant to the substance of our investigation." jordan's letter asked benavides, by then a senior risk manager at amazon, to sit for a transcribed interview.

the shadow government line

patel's post also invoked a private message floris sent during an unrelated episode. floris wrote she was "basically running a shadow government" in september 2020, as the bureau recalled a report alleging chinese election interference, according to fbi messages declassified in july and reported by the washington examiner.

wray named floris in 2022 to run the washington field office's intelligence division, and patel forced her out of the fbi in may 2025, the examiner reported. attorney general pam bondi had already disbanded the task force in february 2025, one of her first acts in office.

the cr-15 squad patel cited at the end of his post was a washington field office public corruption unit that worked arctic frost, the probe that fed into jack smith's election case against trump. patel abolished it last october after disclosures that arctic frost had tracked republican senators' phone records.

the alleged lies date to 2023, according to patel, which keeps them inside the five-year statute of limitations that generally governs federal false-statement charges until 2028. anything the pair did during the 2020 campaign itself fell outside that window last fall.

title: Melania Trump 'Brokers' Oleshky Ceasefire - But The White House And Russia Give Different Start Dates
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Melania Trump 'Brokers' Oleshky Ceasefire - But The White Ho
hay:
melania trump 'brokers' oleshky ceasefire - but the white house and russia give different start dates melania trump 'brokers' oleshky ceasefire - but the white house and russia give different start dates

the white house said friday that first lady melania trump brokered a localized ceasefire in oleshky, a russian-occupied city in ukraine's kherson region, to let aid in and civilians out. the white house says it starts october 29, but gen. valery gerasimov said russian forces would stop firing october 27.

in its statement, the white house said "both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway." melania trump called oleshky "a front-line war city on the brink of disaster" and said she anticipates "some will want to go to russia, and some to ukraine." civilian leaders from both countries are to visit residents in their homes, and an "impartial american media organization" will document the work. reuters reported that newsmax said its cameras would get "exclusive access to document the effort."

moscow's account is looser. gerasimov said fire would cease on the kherson axis at 4 a.m. moscow time on tuesday, and that russia would first carry out "engineering reconnaissance" and secure a humanitarian convoy's route into the city, ap reported. kremlin spokesman dmitry peskov said the sides were still working out a ceasefire so residents could leave, according to the kyiv independent. peskov did not say whether evacuees would go to russian- or ukrainian-held territory, and said the evacuation would likely take several days.

the talks themselves ran through human rights officials. dmytro lubinets, ukraine's ombudsman, said he led negotiations for ukraine and that russia's rights commissioner, yana lantratova, led them for russia. lubinets said the operation would be gradual and "extremely challenging to implement." the white house release casts melania trump as "exclusive intermediary" who "initiated discussions with both nations," but what she did in the room is not spelled out. the daily beast noted this week that her role in the oleshky crisis was unclear. kremlin aide yuri ushakov told reporters putin asked envoy steve witkoff in st. petersburg to pass on his "gratitude," and peskov said the matter came up in a recent putin-trump call.

oleshky sits on the dnipro across from kherson. about 24,000 people lived there before the war; the white house puts the remaining population at 1,700 to 2,000, mostly elderly, with about 50 children. ap described a city with no electricity, heat or running water, scarce food and medicine for months, and mined roads out. the kyiv independent adds that the roads would need demining before buses could reach it. russian forces took the city on the first day of the 2022 invasion, and the june 2023 kakhovka dam collapse, which an ap investigation found was likely caused by the russian military, flooded it and killed hundreds.

pressure had been building for weeks. the kyiv independent says the blockade drew appeals from pope leo xiv, and ukrainian negotiator david arakhamia thanked both the pope and melania trump. ukraine has repeatedly asked for a local ceasefire to organize evacuations; as the occupying power, russia is obligated under international law to see that civilians under its control have what they need to survive, ap noted.

local truces in this war have often been poorly implemented, the kyiv independent notes, and the last one washington announced is a warning. when trump declared an energy ceasefire on truth social earlier this month, zelensky said it was "news to me." zelensky said russia hit at least six energy targets overnight after the announcement, and trump then said both sides had violated the deal and that they agreed "because i said: 'you agree.'"

the announcement lands amid strain between washington and kyiv. trump recently waived new russian sanctions and agreed with russia to import diesel, ap reported, while kyiv faces restrictions on its use of starshield satellite internet. zelensky, speaking at the hudson institute, did not mention oleshky; he said u.s. patriot interceptors were still on hold. witkoff met zelensky in oslo before traveling to see putin.

melania trump has made children caught in the war her signature issue. last october she said she and putin had an open channel of communication on the subject, after the president hand-delivered her letter to putin in alaska. her top aide, marc beckman, has claimed she facilitated the reunification of 34 children with their parents, the daily beast reported.

skeptics are not waiting for the paperwork. stefan vorontsov, a volunteer coordinator at the ngo humanity, told the kyiv independent he worried about "provocations, blackmail, a route through the russian federation." "i have little faith," he said. russia's october 27 date arrives tuesday; the white house's is two days after that.

title: Rare Earth Stocks Hit 52-Week Low As William Blair Says China Supply Optimism Is "Incorrect"
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Rare Earth Stocks Hit 52-Week Low As William Blair Says Chin
hay:
rare earth stocks hit 52-week low as william blair says china supply optimism is "incorrect" rare earth stocks hit 52-week low as william blair says china supply optimism is "incorrect"

our "great rare earth disconnect" note earlier this week highlighted the widening gap between elevated rare earth prices and tumbling junior miners and producers. william blair rare-earths analyst neal dingmann has also weighed in on the forces driving the selloff.

"revived rate-hike fears, hot cpi, and other macro concerns along with rare earth headline and company-specific concerns have notably hurt the largely high-beta rare earth group in recent weeks," dingmann wrote.

the vaneck rare earth and strategic metals etf (remx) has lost more than half its value since peaking in may, even as commodity prices remain strong and demand for conflict-free chinese supplies continues. that divergence raises one key question: how much of the selloff reflects deteriorating fundamentals, and how much reflects misplaced expectations of easing supply constraints?

dingmann wrote that investors may be overestimating the relief a thaw in us-china relations would bring.

"specifically, many investors anticipate (incorrectly, in our opinion) cooling rare earth supply-scarcity with improved u.s./china relations ahead of the next trump/xi meetings in november (in china) and december (g20 in florida)," he said.

he continued:

further, investors appear to have increased liquidity concerns given heavy spending requirements against minimal near-term revenue and milestone-based government funding that for many companies has yet to be collected.

while we continue to point to strong ree prices and potential long-term volumes, many companies are not yet benefiting from the high levels given limited current output at the mine or processing, alloy, and magnet facilities.

while we continue to believe the insatiable demand for ree provides a strong long-term backdrop for much of the group, driving many of our outperform ratings, we remain cautious in the near term over much of the group given the large stock price declines in many ree companies, as it adds to near-term liquidity concerns.

we continue to favor mp materials and lynas rare earths most in the near term given the former's attractive offtake agreements and price floors along with the latter's limited funding needs and long-term track record.

the firm's basket of seven miner stocks (mp, lysdy, arec, ipx, nb, uamy, and tmcr) has tumbled about 30% on average over the previous month at the time of the report. he said interest rate concerns, inflation pressures and expectations of improving us-china relations have compounded worries about spending requirements and delayed government funding.

lower share prices are fueling another major concern for these miners: equity financing is more costly for companies building capital-intensive mines, processing plants and magnet facilities. he warned that some of these miners could hit a "debt wall," substantial shareholder dilution or material project delays.

what changed with investors?

investors appear to continue to shift their focus from upside driven by government support and strategic value toward actual production and cash flow, causing growing concerns about how capital-intensive projects will be funded at lower equity values.

with equity prices significantly lower, raising the capital needed to fund these projects becomes increasingly dilutive, leaving companies that still require significant external funding with fewer options.

from here, we could see a rebound if chinese restrictions are renewed, government funding, or company-specific production milestones restore urgency to the ex-china buildout. on the flip side, another trade extension, company project delays, or funding delays could keep valuations under pressure and further increase funding risk, dilution risk, and overall company finance risk

canaccord's critical minerals team, led by reg spencer, also questioned the scale of the selloff, highlighting the disconnect between elevated rare earth prices and sharp declines across junior miner and established producer stocks.

potential catalysts for renewed investor interest across the space include tighter chinese export restrictions, government funding commitments and production milestones that demonstrate commercial progress. until then, balance-sheet strength and execution remain key differentiators. producers with operating assets and robust liquidity to fund their growth plans appear better positioned to weather the shakeout and participate in a recovery once bears are down and dragging the space down.

title: Measles Surge In Pennsylvania Prompts New Warning
snippet: Measles Surge In Pennsylvania Prompts New Warning
hay:
measles surge in pennsylvania prompts new warning measles surge in pennsylvania prompts new warning

authored by zachary stieber via the epoch times,

as the measles outbreak in pennsylvania grows larger, state officials have issued a warning regarding the impact of measles during pregnancy.

"measles in pregnancy can lead to serious adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. the measles, mumps, and rubella (mmr) vaccine is safe and highly effective," the pennsylvania department of health said in an oct. 19 health alert. "getting vaccinated before pregnancy is the best way to prevent measles and congenital measles."

more cases of measles have been recorded recently during pregnancy, and there are "rising concerns" about congenital measles, or measles transmitted to infants from pregnant mothers, the department said.

women and teenagers in outbreak areas should receive two doses of the mmr vaccine, separated by 28 days, according to the department. other women should be offered one dose.

women should take care not to become pregnant for at least 28 days after receiving a shot.

the u.s. centers for disease control and prevention says that pregnant women should not receive the mmr vaccine. pennsylvania's guidance says the vaccine should not be administered during pregnancy.

infants born to women who had measles are at risk for symptomatic and transmissible measles infection, pennsylvania officials said. infants should be isolated, monitored, and provided with immune globulin, which could prevent measles or reduce symptoms.

infants showing symptoms within 10 days of birth, such as rash, should be tested, and treatment should include vitamin a, since vitamin a deficiency has been linked with poorer outcomes from measles, they said.

cases jump in state

after the alert, pennsylvania officials said the outbreak's case count rose to 1,317.

thirty-one of those cases were new, according to the oct. 21 update.

all but four of those individuals had not received a vaccine, according to the pennsylvania department of health.

five people who contracted measles have died. that includes at least one death that a coroner deemed unrelated to measles.

a one-year-old is held by his mother while he receives a measles vaccine at a clinic in lubbock, texas, on march 1, 2025. jan sonnenmair/getty images

the cdc lists three of the deaths on its website. the cdc said the number may change as it reviews information it has received.

the cdc is also working with a group of epidemiologists to develop a case definition for deaths due to measles.

nationwide, there have been 4,410 measles cases this year, 96 percent of which have occurred in people who are unvaccinated or have unknown vaccination status. ten percent of the patients have been hospitalized.

vaccination effort

about 300 state workers are teaming up with community organizations and health care providers to combat the outbreak by providing factual information and access to the mmr vaccine, the pennsylvania department of health said.

state workers have administered more than 6,300 shots across hundreds of pop-up clinics since the outbreak started in april. they've administered more than 3,700 shots in other venues this year.

healthcare workers are reporting increased interest in the vaccine.

they usually administered about 25,000 doses a month. in september, more than 56,000 doses were injected, and through the first three weeks of october, 39,000 doses have been administered.

the vaccine is estimated to provide 97 percent protection after two doses. side effects include fever and rash.

title: Trump Admin Asks Supreme Court To Allow Border Wall Construction In Texas
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Trump Admin Asks Supreme Court To Allow Border Wall Construc
hay:
trump admin asks supreme court to allow border wall construction in texas trump admin asks supreme court to allow border wall construction in texas

authored by troy myers via the epoch times,

the trump administration has petitioned the supreme court to allow border wall construction to resume in the big bend area of texas.

in an emergency application filed with the high court on oct. 21, lawyers for the federal government asked the justices to lift a lower court order halting construction of president donald trump's key project that began during his first term in office.

in the oct. 3 order, u.s. district judge kathleen cardone sided with environmental groups who claimed the work was unconstitutional, breached the separation of powers, and took land from residents.

"this case involves a baseless injunction that halts a major portion of the construction of the border wall," u.s. solicitor general d. john sauer wrote in the emergency application. "leaving a 300-plus-mile gap in border defenses would act as a dangerous magnet for cartels and other bad actors to exploit as other routes close off."

the trump administration argued that continuing construction was crucial because the big bend region encompasses nearly one-quarter of the u.s. - mexico border.

between fiscal years 2021 and 2025, customs and border protection (cbp) apprehended more than 89,000 foreign nationals attempting to enter through the big bend sector, according to the emergency application, "and those are just the aliens who were detected."

according to cbp data, there were 11,823 apprehensions in the region during 2023 and 3,096 in 2025.

cbp has seized increasing amounts of illegal narcotics across the southwest border, and the sinaloa and juarez cartels, which operate south of the big bend area, continuously seek to exploit any vulnerabilities in the u.s. border to further drug, human, and weapons trafficking, sauer stated.

he argued that cardone's order, if allowed to remain in place, would lead to a number of harms for the federal government, including a disruption of its ability to secure a large portion of the southern border against cartel incursions and activity in addition to irreversible delays, costs, and operational harms from halting already-begun construction.

sauer accused cardone of misbalancing the equities and harms in her ruling.

the judge had conceded the federal government "will experience at least some degree of irreparable harm" because of her block. nonetheless, cardone "illogically concluded" the environmentalist groups' harms outweighed the government's, sauer said.

"the notion that respondents' interest in 'escaping from modern life' in the 'wild spaces in the big bend sector' and preserving 'the spiritual, recreational, and aesthetic value of the area,' surpasses the united states' paramount interest in preventing a quarter of the border from becoming a magnet for cartel exploitation defies credulity," the solicitor general wrote.

plans for border construction in the big bend region were announced in january, with administration officials waiving environmental laws to speed up the building.

the plaintiffs, the center for biological diversity, nonprofit friends of the ruidosa church, and rio grande river guide and landowner in the big bend area danny william miller, filed suit in april over the department of homeland security's (dhs) waiving of regulations.

zeynep graves, a senior attorney at the center for biological diversity, told the epoch times via email that she and the groups are confident the supreme court will hand down a favorable decision.

"we're deeply disappointed that the trump administration is asking the supreme court for a green light to bulldoze one of america's wildest, most extraordinary landscapes," graves said. "once big bend's canyons, cultural treasures and wild ecosystems are destroyed, they'll be lost forever."

by early october, cardone had sided with the groups.

but sauer argued in the emergency application that she never had jurisdiction to issue such a ruling.

he cited a section of the illegal immigration reform and immigrant responsibility act of 1996.

through that legislation, congress granted authority to the attorney general and secretary of dhs to construct border security measures while making it "harder for federal judges to block those critical national security endeavors."

congress also allowed the dhs secretary to waive legal requirements he deemed necessary to ensure speedy construction of roadways and barriers.

to further guard against delays of border wall construction, sauer said, congress "stripped federal courts of jurisdiction to hear any non-constitutional challenges to" a dhs secretary's waiver decisions.

under that authority, homeland security secretary markwayne mullin issued two waivers in 2026 to expedite construction on border walls and roadways in big bend.

"the president received a mandate from the american people to build a wall, defeat the cartels, and stop the flow of illegal aliens and dangerous drugs like fentanyl into our country," dhs general counsel james percival wrote in a post on x. "[cardone's] order is as unprecedented as it is flawed, and we look forward to the supreme court's expeditious consideration of this important question."

however, graves told the epoch times she believed that the lower court does have authority to resolve the groups' claims, and "only congress can authorize something as consequential as walling off the entire u.s. - mexico border."

cbp commissioner rodney scott said he expects the border wall to be completed by the end of 2027.

title: Hegseth Barred Trans Troops - Yet Navy And Marine Boards Are Voting To Keep Them
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Hegseth Barred Trans Troops - Yet Navy And Marine Boards Are
hay:
hegseth barred trans troops - yet navy and marine boards are voting to keep them hegseth barred trans troops - yet navy and marine boards are voting to keep them

military boards set up to push transgender troops out of the service are instead voting to keep many of them, the new york times reported friday, in a quiet break with defense secretary pete hegseth's ban.

nine of the 12 service members who have come before the boards have been approved to stay, according to the times. boards at marine corps base quantico, assigned to carry out the removals, "were doing the opposite," the paper said, and navy boards given strict instructions to force out sailors were "voting to let them stay." a marine staff sergeant who appeared in august thought his career was over, and the panel approved him.

the air force is the exception. the times found no similar pattern there, where transgender airmen are being discharged quickly. the pentagon has not said how many hearings have been held or how many people have been removed, and the proceedings are closed, even to spouses.

rachel vanlandingham, a former air force lawyer now at southwestern law school, told the times the boards "are being told to do something that they know is wrong."

the boards are the last step in a removal campaign that began with a january 2025 executive order. in a september 2025 speech at quantico, hegseth told troops, "no more identity months, dei offices, dudes in dresses." the supreme court let the ban take effect on may 6, 2025, and hegseth's may 8 memo gave active-duty troops until june 6 and reservists until july 7 to leave voluntarily before involuntary separation began. pentagon data from december 2024 counted about 4,240 service members with a gender dysphoria diagnosis.

the boards were designed to reach one result. priya rashid, a military attorney who represents transgender service members, told npr in february that the outcome is "generally predetermined" and put the cost of assembling each board at $22,000.

an october 2025 pentagon memo lets commanders overturn a board's decision to let a transgender service member stay. the memo, from undersecretary anthony tata and obtained by ap, breaks with longstanding policy that boards act independently. it also requires transgender troops to appear in uniforms matching their birth sex, and a hearing proceeds without them if they refuse.

title: Gen X And Boomer Progressives Are Conditioned To Support Open Borders
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Gen X And Boomer Progressives Are Conditioned To Support Ope
hay:
gen x and boomer progressives are conditioned to support open borders gen x and boomer progressives are conditioned to support open borders

authored by andrew devine via the daily sceptic,

left-leaning boomers (born 1946-1964) and gen xers (born 1965-1980) view any criticism of 21st century mass immigration through a particular cultural and psychological lens that is outdated and a barrier to having a constructive debate about extremist mass immigration policies in the here and now.

left-liberal 'progressives' who grew up or were young adults between the 1960s and 1990s were socially and culturally conditioned to believe that any criticism of immigration policies is synonymous with racial hatred. this is because in the eras when they grew up many of the people who opposed the much more limited immigration of those decades were openly racist. this is why it's almost impossible to have a nuanced discussion with 'progressive' boomers or gen x about the issue of mass immigration and get them to address the reality of resource constraints caused by excessively high numbers, or how certain immigrant groups like indian sikhs or middle eastern christians are a better cultural fit with british and european people than say an afghan taliban supporter or an islamic supremacist from somalia who openly promotes female genital mutilation as beneficial to society.

the moment a boomer or gen x leftist open borders advocate is faced with anyone critical of 21st century mass immigration policies (which are radically more open than the immigration policies of the 1950s-1980s) all they see and hear in their mind's eye is some frothing at the mouth national front extremist skinhead from the 1970s or 1980s who believes there shouldn't be a single brown or black face on the island of britain. unless you can break through that cultural and psychological conditioning regarding the issue of immigration, it's impossible to have a constructive debate with 'progressive' gen xers and boomers on the issue. while you're trying to have a nuanced discussion on the issue of mass immigration, left-liberal boomers and gen xers are having a pavlovian response.

in order to understand the psychology of gen x and boomer british 'progressives' further, it's important to understand that we are the generations who grew up listening to music that transcended cultural and racial lines. we grew up listening to motown and philly soul from black america along with black musical giants like prince, michael jackson or james brown, while even all-white bands like the rolling stones, the beatles, the who and later u2 paid homage to the black r&b artists who inspired them. in the late 1970s and early 1980s, the 2-tone music label fused white british punk rock with jamaican ska and reggae and the label's multi-ethnic bands such as the specials topped the charts. it was the norm for us to see black, brown and white musicians in bands together. for those who love football, many black footballers born and bred in england and even ireland were viewed as belonging to the country as much as any white player. this inclusive ethos that was prevalent in the 1970s and 1980s that emphasised black, white and brown kids uniting in a love of music, fashion and football was all very laudable and it helped foster a cultural norm where genuine racism came to be viewed as anathema by most of the public.

however, the inclusiveness of the 1970s and 1980s led many of the people who adopted this mindset to adopt a very simplistic and shallow minded approach to the issue of immigration which is now influencing how we discuss the very different phenomenon of mass immigration in the 21st century. the gen x or boomer 'progressive' erroneously conflates criticism of any non-white, non-european culture with racism which in turn has led to the idea that to oppose unrestricted flows of people with darker skin from all of the world's non-white cultures is synonymous with white supremacy. this is the mindset that has dominated most of the british media and cultural establishment for decades. it shapes everything from how certain news items are reported (or not reported). it explains why tv dramas include the over representation of ethnic minorities even in periods and locations in british history where everyone was white along with the incongruous shoe-horning of radical-leftist dogma into so much modern entertainment.

it must be infuriating for decent, law-abiding caribbeans, african christians and indians who came to the british isles many decades ago and are patriotic and well-integrated to be lumped in with islamic supremacists coming from afghanistan or somalia just because they're all non-white. leftists are so obsessed with skin colour and viewing 21st century mass immigration through the racial politics of the 1970s and 1980s that it blinds them to genuine cultural incompatibilities of certain immigrant groups as well as security threats and resource constraints that result from the 21st century open borders fiasco.

one aspect of the current debate about what it means to be british that needs to be acknowledged is that it was only possible for caribbean or indian migrants who came to britain in the 1950s and 1960s to become culturally british because there was a majority white british population and culture with which to integrate. if you make whole areas of cities non-native british, and especially if those areas become dominated by islamic supremacists, then there is no native culture for people to integrate with. civic nationalism can only work when the indigenous people remain the dominant majority and immigrant groups come from compatible cultures who aspire to integrate with the host population.

boomer and gen x 'progressives' need to wake up to the fact that it's not the mid to late 20th century anymore. they need to have debates on mass immigration in the 21st century on the conditions and terms of the 21st century. today's mass immigration is not comparable to the limited migration of the 1950s through to the 1980s. those of us with centrist or small c conservative views on immigration, including many patriotic ethnic minority citizens, agree with 'progressives' that racism is wrong. where we disagree with them is how they've extended that term and redefined it beyond its original meaning to the point of utter absurdity.

there is nothing racist about effective border controls or wanting manageable levels of immigration that consider resource constraints and security risks. there is nothing far right about believing that the native peoples of the british isles (the english, scottish, welsh, irish and northern irish) should remain the majority in these islands and that only cultures that are compatible with ours should be invited to live amongst us. if we forget that, then the national and regional cultures that have shaped the british isles will disappear.

andrew devine is a 2010 orwell prize winning blogger and author of generation f (under the pseudonym winston smith). former radical leftist. fully recovered. he blogs on his substack page, the devine message, where this article first appeared.

title: Supreme Court Allows New Hampshire To Bar Student IDs At Polls For Midterms
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Supreme Court Allows New Hampshire To Bar Student IDs At Pol
hay:
supreme court allows new hampshire to bar student ids at polls for midterms supreme court allows new hampshire to bar student ids at polls for midterms

authored by matthew vadum via the epoch times,

the supreme court sided with new hampshire republicans, allowing officials to stop accepting student id cards as valid proof of identity for voting.

the high court cited the purcell principle, which guards against changes to election rules close to election day.

the court's decision took the form of an unsigned opinion issued late on oct. 22.

justice ketanji brown jackson dissented.

the supreme court here applied the so-called purcell principle against last-minute judicially ordered changes to election rules.

a state law known as hb 323 forbids the use of student ids as valid proof of identity when voting. new hampshire secretary of state david scanlan issued guidance directing election clerks not to accept student ids as a backup form of identification.

a group called the coalition for open democracy challenged both the state law and the directive in federal court. the group's attorneys argued that the law ran afoul of both the u.s. and new hampshire constitutions and discriminated against young voters on the basis of age. they also argued scanlan exceeded his lawful powers as secretary of state.

earlier this month, u.s. district judge joseph laplante denied the group's request to bar enforcement of hb 323, but temporarily blocked scanlan from advising election clerks that student ids were never acceptable. days later, the judge extended his order to cover public statements to that effect made by scanlan. together, the two orders meant clerks had to keep treating a student id card as possible backup proof.

in its emergency application to the supreme court, the state argued that the district court's order came a mere 32 days before the general election, and that this goes against the supreme court's rulings, which have repeatedly held that lower federal courts should not "intervene in state election procedures in the lead up to an election."

the justices stayed laplante's orders.

"this court has repeatedly emphasized that lower federal courts should ordinarily not alter the election rules on the eve of an election," the justices wrote, citing a 2020 precedent. "here, the district court did not point to anything that would justify deviating from that principle."

in her dissent, jackson said laplante had determined that it was necessary to correct scanlan's "publicized misstatement about what new hampshire's election rules require."

the injunction issued by the district court, jackson said, "was reasonably designed to address alleged misinformation, not to change the law."

"an injunction to prohibit that conduct does not contribute to public confusion, it prevents that very problem," she said. "i would not disturb a clearly justifiable federal-court order issued to ensure that the public receives accurate information about a state's electoral processes."

new hampshire attorney general john formella hailed the supreme court's ruling.

"new hampshire has a responsibility to protect the integrity of its elections and ensure that election laws are applied as written," he said in a statement.

"the supreme court's decision is an important victory for our efforts to defend those laws and prevent last-minute court orders from creating uncertainty for voters and election officials."

the coalition for open democracy criticized the high court's new ruling, calling it "wrong" and a misinterpretation of the purcell principle.

"we applaud justice jackson for her dissent, in which she stands for the constitution, the right to vote, and a rational application of purcell," the group said in a statement.

"we will continue to vigorously litigate this case in the defense of the fundamental right to vote of young voters across new hampshire."

the supreme court's order remains in effect through the nov. 3 general election, while the case continues on appeal in the lower courts.

hay:

amid the record pace in iranian attacks on crude tankers in the strait of hormuz, many have been wondering: where does all that oil end up when it comes to severely damaged or sunken tankers?

on friday the uae has confirmed a deeply alarming event: some of its beaches are being shuttered as a major spill is washing up after a tanker was struck by a projectile off the uae coast, resulting in a fire aboard the vessel and apparent major spillage. the attack incident happened earlier in october.

authorities have "detected a tanker oil spill affecting umm al quwain's beaches," the ministry of climate change and environment announced in a statement.

it confirmed that the emirate in question was forced to close its beaches, and that "teams immediately began containment, cordoning, clean-up and remediation... to limit environmental impacts."

international reports have identified that the leak resulted from the oct.9 incident involving the gem no.2 tanker, which had been detailed by the ukmto

"gem no. 2, was hit by a projectile friday off the coast of the uae resulting in a fire onboard. the ship departed ras tanura, saudi arabia, in march and has remained in the persian gulf since the war began," as reported at the time.

the last week saw increasing complaints by beach area residents of unusual smells - reports that were initially brushed off by local authorities. one regional gulf outlet documents the following timeline:

october 19: unusual smells reported

reports of unusual odours emerged on monday, october 19, in sharjah and other parts of the uae.

the reports prompted authorities to begin monitoring the situation in coordination with federal and local government agencies.

authorities conducted inspections and assessments to identify the source of the smells and determine whether they posed any risk to residents.

october 20: sharjah police reassure residents

lieutenant general abdullah mubarak bin amer, commander-in-chief of sharjah police, addressed public concerns during the direct line programme broadcast on sharjah tv and radio.

he said the situation was safe and stable, with no indication of a threat to public health or safety.

october 21: environment ministry provides initial findings

the ministry said its assessments found no cause for concern.

field monitoring and response efforts were continuing to reduce the odours and help them dissipate.

but then by friday the oil spill impacting beaches was belatedly confirmed. this came long after oil-like smells began to inundate local social media, and government office call centers.

title: Harvard Medical School Holds Panel Raising Whether Weight Loss Drugs Are An Imperialistic, Militaristic Plot
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Harvard Medical School Holds Panel Raising Whether Weight Lo
hay:
harvard medical school holds panel raising whether weight loss drugs are an imperialistic, militaristic plot harvard medical school holds panel raising whether weight loss drugs are an imperialistic, militaristic plot

authored by jonathan turley via jonathanturley.org,

harvard university is facing another controversy after its medical school held an event on "the pathology of unruly bodies." the most surprising part is that it was not a reference to the harvard faculty itself. rather, a panel composed of non-medical experts was railing against anti-obesity drugs as part of "indoctrination" to support the ills of "empire and imperialism." welcome to the state of higher education in america.

the panel was devoid of actual medical experts. it was dressed up in medical terms with the use of the word "pathology." it could have easily been billed as "glp-1 anti-body." the panel included such experts as da'shaun l harrison, who recently drew notoriety for claiming at the socialism 2026 conference in chicago that glp-1 medications constitute "genocide" against fat people.

another headliner was roxane gay, the gloria steinem endowed chair in media, culture, and feminist studies at rutgers university - new brunswick and the artist-in-residence at harvard medical school. professor gay (the cousin of former harvard university president claudine gay) had called for the release of luigi mangione, who murdered brian thompson, the ceo of unitedhealthcare, two years ago.

despite her extremism and penchant for murderers like mangione, gay writes for the new york times and apparently likes to flip off people in public. harvard decided she was exactly what they needed to help shape their medical students. she is part of the radical chic of higher education, where no views are too far left (while departments purge conservatives and libertarians).

harrison quickly picked up where she left off at the socialist convention with bizarre claims. rather than claiming that drug companies were engaging in the genocide of fat people with weight-loss drugs, she explained that the companies were really militarizing an imperialist state: "this practice of forcing people into manipulating and changing or shifting how they look is oftentimes about making bodies militarisable. building up a military to defend an imperialist state."

she further claimed:

"a lot of doctors, medical professionals and folks who collaborate with them - be it through the government or media - are advocating for atrocities that are directly impacting our citizens, but also citizens around the globe.

it then becomes about creating this ideal body that you are always being pushed and pulled towards, as a way to represent this patriotism that is intended to indoctrinate one into the military, into the defense of the country."

the suggestion that weight loss is an imperialist militaristic plot is obviously bonkers. it is the kind of raving you would expect on a subway from someone wearing a handmade cardboard sign and a tin foil hat.

however, harvard medical school views that person as a serious expert on the pathologies of weight loss.

notably, not a single harvard faculty member expressed unease over the programming. medical students are facing an array of tough technological and economic conditions. yet, the administration wants them to sit through far-left indoctrinations from the likes of gay and harrison.

harvard is not alone. various medical schools have incorporated radical social agendas into their curricula or events. we recently discussed how ucla medical school held a panel on which psychiatrists defended self-immolation in protesting israel. in an earlier post, we discussed a mandatory lecture at ucla of one of the university's "activists-in-residence" replete with anti-semitic postings and racist rhetoric.

the hiring of figures like gay and the radical programs at these schools show that faculty have little intention to change the ideological echo chamber in higher education. it is truly a pathology of unruly bodies.

jonathan turley is a law professor and the new york times best-selling author of "rage and the republic: the unfinished story of the american revolution."

title: A Withdrawn Immigration Application, Corrected Tax Returns, And 'Military Officer' Father: Ilhan Omar Evidence Piles Up
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">A Withdrawn Immigration Application, Corrected Tax Returns,
hay:
a withdrawn immigration application, corrected tax returns, and 'military officer' father: ilhan omar evidence piles up a withdrawn immigration application, corrected tax returns, and 'military officer' father: ilhan omar evidence piles up

update (1218et): the new york post has published additional reporting on the disputed allegations surrounding omar's marriage to ahmed elmi, highlighting a british marriage certificate alongside previously reported financial records and witness claims.

omar denies wrongdoing, and the material presented does not establish that elmi is her brother or that their marriage was fraudulent. the post's cited evidence and allegations include:

  • family records and names: a 1997 british marriage certificate obtained by the post identifies the father of leila nur said, whom the paper describes as believed to be omar's sister, as nur said elmi. sources told the paper this was another name used by omar's father. the post also cites the federal filing identifying omar as “ilhan nur said elmi, a/k/a ilhan abdullahi omar.” his profession is listed as "military officer."
  • a shared address: omar and elmi listed the same columbia heights, minnesota, address on their 2009 marriage application. ahmed hirsi, the father of omar's children, also used that address for a business license, according to the post.
  • overlapping relationships and tax filings: omar had her third child with hirsi in 2012 while legally married to elmi. the post also cites joint tax returns omar filed with hirsi for 2014 and 2015, before her divorce from elmi was finalized in 2017. those returns were subsequently corrected.

the trump administration has filed a lawsuit to block certification of the senate race in alaska if republican sen. dan sullivan loses the election while another candidate with the same name is on the ballot.

title: France Braces For Moody's Downgrade As OAT-Bund Spread Hits EU Crisis Level Highs
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">France Braces For Moody's Downgrade As OAT-Bund Spread Hits
hay:
france braces for moody's downgrade as oat-bund spread hits eu crisis level highs france braces for moody's downgrade as oat-bund spread hits eu crisis level highs

france faces a potential credit rating downgrade later today as social unrest, a deteriorating welfare state, a deficit crisis, political paralysis, and years of uncontrolled mass migration collide, forcing the government to repair its finances or risk sparking the next eurozone crisis.

unicredit fixed-income strategist francesco maria di bella told clients earlier, "tonight, moody's will review france's credit rating, which is currently at aa3 with a negative outlook."

di bella outlined his expectations for moody's upcoming ratings decision:

we expect the rating agency to downgrade french public debt as deteriorating fiscal indicators are compounded by political constraints that hinder efforts to place public finances on a more sustainable path.

with s&p and fitch already placing the country's rating credit one notch lower, we think this move is broadly expected and should not lead to a further underperformance of french govies.

the 10y oat-bund spread is currently trading at around 175bp, 90bp wider than at the beginning of september and at the highest level since its peak in november 2011.

that said, a rating downgrade would keep investor attention high on the political uncertainty and weakening economic fundamentals in france.

next year's presidential election represents a source of concern not only for france but for the entire eurozone, and adds to other risk factors such as geopolitical tensions and elevated energy prices.

bank of america co-head of global rates strategy sphia salim wrote in a note:

attention is firmly on risk assets. the equity sell-off, wider credit spreads and oat-bund breakout increasingly reinforce one another, adding momentum to the duration rally alongside the continued short covering by ctas & bid for receivers.

after close, we will also get moody's rating decision for france. if moody's doesn't deliver a downgrade and simply reaffirms the negative outlook, the decision could offer some reprieve to oat-bunds. absent a stabilization in spread, the pressure will be on the ecb to deliver at least some verbal intervention (rates - eu).

france's oat-bund spread widened to 175 bps friday morning, approaching levels seen at the height of the eurozone sovereign debt crisis.

france's cds spreads suggest investors are pricing its sovereign risk more like a low single-a or high-bbb credit.

here's more commentary from cosimo codacci-pisanelli and rikin shah via goldman sachs:

pressure on france builds...

10y oat-bund closed at 173bp on thursday, the widest since november 2011, and france now trades 45bp through italy. the forced deleveraging of two weeks ago has stopped, yet spreads have gone well through the 12-oct highs anyway. this is a fundamentals story, not just a positioning one.

last weekend's protests were the largest since the yellow vests and the 2019/2023 pension strikes, and a post-protest poll now puts melenchon in the second round. the direct growth hit from the riots looks small, but it is another headwind to an already weak growth outlook: gir have downside risks to their 2027 growth forecast 0.6% vs the government's 1.0%. even in the constructive scenario, where the 5.0% 2027 budget deficit target passes by year-end, gir expect the deficit to realise at 5.3% given their weaker growth forecast. the arithmetic is challenging and unforgiving. with an assumption of 1% real growth, 2% inflation and a 4% borrowing cost, stabilising the debt needs a primary surplus of ~1%, something france has rarely come close to (chart). if funding costs converge to where 10y oats trade today, just above 5%, that requirement drifts towards 2%. the bigger takeaway from the protests is that this is not a society ready to accept that scale of adjustment, whatever the political will.

there is undoubtedly a market structure component to the moves too. positioning in the front end has been reduced and changed hands at better levels in the recent sell-off, but is still long. further out the curve, the most striking thing has been the lack of buying.. even fair value models screening oats as ~60bp cheap, value alone hasn't brought real money in. so what turns buying momentum? an energy-relief-driven duration rally might help, as might lower vol. really it needs some fundamental improvement in the outlook... and in the short term that looks challenging, with the calendar showing more potential headwinds than tailwinds: moody's review today, more protests expected this weekend, downside risks to q3 gdp (first print 30 oct), strikes expected on 5th nov and a the melenchon rally on 6th nov. it's hard right now to see a material trigger for a material reversal in spreads, with further widening at risk of becoming even more convex from here. the risk of such moves ahead of clear event risk is enough to deter fair value buyers for now.

france's lower house scrapped key savings measures from the 2027 budget this week, undermining efforts to bring the deficit down to 5% of gdp from 5.4% this year. opposition parties have shown no appetite for compromise ahead of the presidential election, rejecting spending cuts while pushing for additional outlays.

"you want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. that's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread," said rushabh amin, a portfolio manager at allspring global investments.

mike bell of rbc bluebay asset management expects it could get even uglier if moody's, s&p, and fitch all lower france's rating into the bbb category, the lowest investment-grade tier.

title: Dolly Parton's Sister Says Tennessee Machine Kept Defaulting To Blackburn; State Claims "Not A Vote Flipping Situation"
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Dolly Parton's Sister Says Tennessee Machine Kept Defaulting
hay:
dolly parton's sister says tennessee machine kept defaulting to blackburn; state claims "not a vote flipping situation" dolly parton's sister says tennessee machine kept defaulting to blackburn; state claims "not a vote flipping situation"

stella parton, dolly parton's younger sister, says a voting machine at the hermitage library in davidson county kept selecting republican gubernatorial nominee marsha blackburn, a candidate she says she would never vote for, forcing her to correct her ballot three times. mediaite flagged her post. tennessee's elections coordinator calls such reports unintended touches, and says the paper ballot, not the screen, is what gets counted.

"in tennessee last week at the hermitage library where i voted, i had to go back three times and correct my vote because it kept defaulting to marsha blackburn," parton wrote on facebook. "don't let them rig this election." blackburn, a sitting u.s. senator, faces democrat jerri green, a memphis city councilmember, in the governor's race.

parton said she finally called over a poll worker on the third try, and she urged voters to "double check your ballot before you print it out and put it through the machine." it's unclear whether the problem was a malfunction, user error or something else.

she is not the only one. wsmv reported on oct. 20 that jackie herrud, who voted at the longview recreation center in spring hill in neighboring williamson county, said, "i kept punching for the democrat, jerri green, and it kept punching back to marsha blackburn." poll workers there told her they had heard similar complaints. another williamson county voter, toni fitzgerald, said the button was hard to press and she kept pressing until it registered; her site had no stylus.

in response, tennessee's secretary of state's office said it had received one matching complaint out of about 400,000 voters as of that oct. 20 report, and pointed to the selection screen, the review screen and the paper record as safeguards. more calls came in after the story aired.

by the next day, elections coordinator mark goins told wsmv: "it's not a vote flipping situation. it's normally like an unintended touch that they may not even realize." he added, "in all the situations, since i've been here, that's exactly what's occurred." goins said the marking device stores no votes, and the paper ballot is what gets counted. "they're actually being counted on that paper ballot that's going in the scanner," he said. wsmv reported that davidson and williamson counties use ballot marking machines, while other counties use different equipment.

for each reported problem, goins said, his office contacts the county and sends one republican and one democratic technician to examine the machine. neither wsmv report describes the results of any such inspection.

davidson county elections administrator john richardson told wsmv that about 65,000 people had voted early in the county and only a few had called with concerns. the county is bringing back stir sticks, which work as styluses, because "when they use their finger it doesn't necessarily connect." it used them in 2024 and dropped them over plastic-use concerns. richardson told newschannel 5 the touchscreens, in use for about a decade, respond to pressure, so fingers or nails can be less precise. a davidson county voter there, gladys mccowen, said she pressed the middle of jerri green's name and blackburn's appeared, but her paper ballot was accurate. blackburn urged voters to report irregularities to their local election commission, and green's campaign manager said voters had reported switching away from green.

tennessee has been here before. at an aug. 5 press conference held jointly by shelby county's democratic and republican parties and the memphis naacp, naacp member gale jones carson said a machine selected a different candidate than the one she chose, and that it took three tries. separately, the county election commission blamed "human error" for one early voting machine in bartlett that omitted four state judicial races for 307 voters. in 2024, shelby county officials said they found no irregularities after similar claims, and in texas, tarrant county said one of 58,000 first-day ballots was misprinted due to voter error, cbs news reported at the time.

** press release ** pic.twitter.com/yc5gazwnet

— tarrant county elections (@tarrantelection) october 22, 2024

calibration is the likeliest technical explanation on offer. an election expert told the center for an informed public at the university of washington there are known calibration issues with some older touchscreens, including some used in tennessee. no cause has been established for any of the tennessee reports, and no independent inspection of the machines has been published.

mediaite also cited nashville turnout "15 times higher" than the 2022 midterm. wpln reported that figure compares first-day in-person voting, up about 1,400% from 607 voters at the city's sole polling site in 2022. with mail ballots the increase is about 240%, and against the 2018 governor's race, first-day turnout fell nearly 20%. early voting runs through oct. 29, and election day is nov. 3.

title: New York City Votes To Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages, Ending 170-Year Tradition
snippet: <span property="schema:name" class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">New York City Votes To Ban Horse-Drawn Carriages, Ending 170
hay:
new york city votes to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending 170-year tradition new york city votes to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending 170-year tradition

authored by kimberly hayek via the epoch times,

the new york city council voted on thursday to pass romanch's law, phasing out horse-drawn carriages in central park by june 1, 2028.

forty council members voted yes. twenty-nine had signed onto the bill sponsored by council member christopher marte. speaker julie menin is the first sitting speaker to support such a ban.

"today, the city council made history. our landmark vote to pass romanch's law is a demonstration of this council's commitment to animal welfare, public safety, and worker protection," menin said in a statement.

the law bars new licenses on or after june 1, 2028. existing ones expire permanently on may 31, 2028. the law requires the mayor's administration to create a workforce transition program by april 1, 2027, which includes job referrals, career counseling, hiring fairs, and educational opportunities.

it also considers compensation for owners based on business value, licenses, and equipment. horses must be certified by june 1, 2027, not to be sold for slaughter or other inhumane purposes, and owners may keep them.

a joint working group will include one representative each from the speaker's office, the administration, and labor.

the vote followed the june death of 18-year-old romanch mahajan, a tourist from india.

on june 17, mahajan fell from a carriage after the horse spooked and bolted during a ride with his family. mahajan hit his head and died. after his death, menin announced her support for the ban in a video on x.

"the tragic and preventable death of 18-year-old romanch mahajan made clear that the status quo is no longer acceptable," menin said oct. 14 when announcing the oct. 22 full council vote on the measure.

mahajan's death was the first in more than 160 years of horse-drawn carriages operating under the transport workers union, which represents the carriage drivers, in the park.

mayor zohran mamdani confirmed he and the speaker had agreed to the june 1, 2028, end date.

"i think that we have a civic responsibility to ensure that we are not leaving anybody out to dry," mamdani said at an unrelated press conference on oct. 14.

the transport workers union denounced the text of the bill as noncommittal, with "no meaningful economic relief for workers."

the bill does not require the city to compensate the 68 owners for their city-issued licenses or medallions.

in a statement, the union denounced menin for what it described as using "the tragic death of a tourist to contrive a public safety crisis."

president donald trump, who is from new york city, criticized the ban on truth social, writing: "so sad to see the beloved central park horse-drawn carriage industry ending after over a century, based largely on one tragic accident. when there is a car accident in the area, of which there are many, they don't stop cars from entering the park. so why would they stop the carriages? it was a great tradition. another piece of history that's gone. it will be missed!"

in a separate post, he added, "the horse-drawn carriage in new york city is a quintessential new york experience. so sad that, for political reasons, we will see it go!"

animal rights group new yorkers for clean, livable, and safe streets (nyclass) reacted on x to the ban.

"for decades, nyclass fought to end cruel and dangerous horse carriages," it wrote. "it took the extraordinary courage, compassion, and unwavering leadership of speaker menin."

horse-drawn carriages have operated in central park since 1858. they began as transportation and became a tourist attraction.

council member tony avella introduced the first ban legislation in 2007. later efforts, including under mayor bill de blasio in 2014, failed. ryder's law after a 2022 horse collapse also did not pass. council member robert holden reintroduced a version in november 2025 focused on workforce programs, which also stalled.

carriage license owner ahmet bilici, who trained as a veterinarian in turkey before coming to the united states in 2001, became a carriage driver to support himself as he was learning english.

the job stuck, and he's been a driver for 23 years. he said that if the city council wanted to work with carriage drivers, drivers would be amenable, but he said the city council just wants a ban.

"when you take this carriage from me, i am going to lose my quarter century! no way!" he previously told the epoch times. "i trusted the city because the city licensed the medallion, and now you are shutting down? no way!"

bilici said the ban will hurt 300 families including support staff such as stable workers, blacksmiths producing horseshoes, and craftsmen making saddles.

"this is my small business, my investment. it's like my house. you're burning my house!" he said. "there's no way we can accept this."

another driver, danielle slot, also said she was extremely disappointed. she said she thinks there is no solid justification for the ban.

"our city council is supposed to look out for people and represent people, and they're supposed to see through these things," slot previously told the epoch times, referring to the long-term campaign of nyclass head steven nislick to ban carriage horses, which dates to 2008.

"i've just completely lost faith in the government here, which is very sad," she said. "it feels like they're capitalizing on sensationalism.

"it's a really nice thought that there would be some magical sanctuary [for the horses]. but it's just not realistic."

city rules currently limit horses to nine-hour workdays, five weeks of annual vacation, and prohibit work when temperatures are below 18 degrees or above 90 degrees.

for more than three decades, michael gove has been a leading figure in british conservatism. as a journalist, government minister and now editor of the tory bible, the spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. in the latest episode of radical thinking, gove joins aditya chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on brexit and austerity, and the spectator’s position on islam

watch the full episode with michael gove here.

aditya’s suggested reading:

to read the fruits of michael gove’s dalliance with the marxism today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called the moderniser’s dilemma: radical politics in the age of blair

for slalom ride through michael gove’s years in power, read the demented dalek by the historian richard j evans in the london review of books

to learn more on what’s become of the british right, there’s a column by me for the guardian

just why the most successful political party is now failing is analysed in-depth by phil burton-cartledge in his book the party’s over: the rise and fall of the conservatives from thatcher to sunak

phil also writes a very good blog on british politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. here he is on kemi badenoch
